name: Earthquakes and early warning
description: Earthquake products and decisions: the event summary, PAGER, aftershock forecasts, early warning alerts and the automated actions they trigger, building safety placards and lifeline status. For seismic networks, early warning operations and every organization that has buildings, people and lifelines in shaking.
outsideParties: the regional seismic network and the national earthquake information center
early warning delivery partners (phone alerts, apps)
the state or county building department
the utility operations center (power, gas, water)
the transportation department and rail operators

advisorRoles.name: Duty Seismologist (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Explains magnitudes, ShakeMap and PAGER, and the aftershock forecast to the players.

advisorRoles.name: Building Inspector Lead (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Applies safety placards and explains re-entry rules for damaged buildings.

glossary.definition: Moment magnitude, energy at the source, one number per earthquake (M 6.8). The first automatic value is revised within minutes to hours.
Modified Mercalli shaking at a place, Roman numerals I to X. Differs by place and falls with distance. A different scale from magnitude.
ShakeMap maps estimated shaking; PAGER estimates fatalities and economic loss, each with a color alert (green, yellow, orange, red). Versions rise as data arrive.
An alert sent after rupture begins, seconds to tens of seconds before strong shaking. Near the epicenter it can arrive after shaking starts (blind zone).
Probability of at least one aftershock above a magnitude (3, 5, 6, 7) in a window (day, week, month, year), with expected ranges. Not a prediction of when.
Building safety tag: INSPECTED (green), RESTRICTED USE (yellow), UNSAFE (red); the word always appears.

productConventions: Magnitude is M 6.8 (decimal); intensity is a Roman numeral MMI (VII). Never swap them.
Mark an event automatic or reviewed; a later magnitude differs from the first by 0.1 to 0.5.
Phone early warning alerts: M 5.0+ with expected MMI IV+; app alerts M 4.5+ with MMI III+. Text: Earthquake! Drop, Cover, Hold On.
realismRules: No warning time for places within about 20 to 30 km of the epicenter; the alert can be late there. Strong shaking travels about 3.5 km per second.
Aftershock chances are probabilities and ranges. A larger earthquake than the mainshock is possible but unlikely. Nobody can say aftershocks have ended.
The building department places placards. A green placard is not a guarantee against aftershocks.
Lifelines are restored in stages, not all at once.
